# Generated code

The output is a TypeScript codebase organised by proto package, one concept per
file, with snake_case file names that mirror the proto. Every file starts with
the protokit header:

```ts
// Code generated by protoc-gen-codemode. DO NOT EDIT.
// versions:
// 	protoc-gen-codemode v0.1.0
// 	protoc (unknown)
// source: library/v1/book.proto
//
// codemode — https://github.com/the-protobuf-project/codemode
```

## Folder structure

```
gen/
  index.ts                                export * as libraryV1; catalog, config, connectors
  codemode/
    catalog.ts                            what search() and describe() read
    config.ts                             runtime settings from codemode.yaml
    index.ts                              Services interface and connectors()
    sandbox.d.ts                          everything sandboxed code can use, in one file
  library/v1/
    index.ts                              the package, and Any registration of its codecs
    messages/book.ts                      interface Book, BookCodec
    messages/book_edition.ts              nested messages are flattened: Book.Edition -> BookEdition
    enums/book_state.ts                   type BookState, BookStateCodec
    resources/book_name.ts                type BookName and its format/parse helper
    services/library_service/
      service.ts                          interface LibraryService, LibraryServiceDescriptor
      client.ts                           class LibraryServiceClient implements LibraryService
      connector.ts                        libraryServiceConnector(service)
      index.ts
```

Well-known types come from the runtime package rather than being generated.

## Interfaces

Interfaces follow protojson exactly, so the model, the sandbox boundary, the
client and your code share one shape:

| Proto | TypeScript |
| --- | --- |
| `int32`, `uint32`, `float`, `double` | `number` |
| `int64`, `uint64` and fixed variants | `string` (exact) |
| `bytes` | `string` (base64) |
| enum | union of value names |
| resource name field | template literal, e.g. `` `shelves/${string}` `` |
| `repeated T`, `map<K, V>` | `T[]`, `Record<string, V>` |
| `Timestamp`, `Duration`, `FieldMask` | `string` |
| `Struct`, `Value`, `ListValue` | `JsonObject`, `JsonValue`, `JsonValue[]` |
| wrappers | `T \| null` |
| `Any`, `Empty` | `AnyMessage`, `Empty` |

Fields are optional unless `REQUIRED`. Oneof members are optional fields whose
JSDoc names the oneof; `fromJson` rejects a message that sets two of them.

## Codecs

Each message has a `MessageCodec<T>`:

- `fromJson(json, path?)` validates protojson, accepts proto field names too,
  fills defaults, and throws `INVALID_ARGUMENT` with a path such as
  `library.v1.Book.editions[0].year`.
- `toJson(message, { emitDefaults? })` leaves out defaults, unless asked;
  connectors emit them, so sandboxed code can read `page.books.length` on an
  empty page.
- `encode(message, writer?)` and `decode(bytes | reader, length?)` speak the
  protobuf binary format, for Connect binary and storage.

`toBinary`, `fromBinary`, `toJsonString` and `fromJsonString` wrap them.

## Clients and transports

```ts
const http = new LibraryServiceClient(httpTransport({ baseUrl, headers: { authorization } }));
const connect = new LibraryServiceClient(connectTransport({ baseUrl, format: "binary" }));
const binding = new LibraryServiceClient(connectTransport({ baseUrl: "https://internal", fetch: env.LIBRARY.fetch.bind(env.LIBRARY) }));
```

`connectHandler([{ descriptor: LibraryServiceDescriptor, impl }])` serves an
implementation over Connect as a fetch handler: `Bun.serve`, `Deno.serve`, a
Worker, or a test.

## Templates

The layout of every generated file lives in
[`plugin/generator/templates/typescript`](../plugin/generator/templates/typescript), one `*.tpl` per
file kind, embedded in the plugin:

| Template | Writes |
| --- | --- |
| `message.ts.tpl`, `interface.tpl` | `messages/<name>.ts`: the interface and its codec |
| `enum.ts.tpl`, `enum.tpl` | `enums/<name>.ts` |
| `resource.ts.tpl`, `resource.tpl` | `resources/<name>.ts` |
| `service.ts.tpl`, `client.ts.tpl`, `connector.ts.tpl`, `service_index.ts.tpl` | `services/<name>/` |
| `package_index.ts.tpl`, `codemode_index.ts.tpl`, `root_index.ts.tpl` | the `index.ts` files |
| `catalog.ts.tpl`, `config.ts.tpl`, `sandbox.d.ts.tpl`, `sandbox.tpl` | `codemode/` |

Templates are presentation only. The generator resolves every name, type and
expression, adds the imports they need, and passes the result in as a view
struct; templates arrange it. `interface.tpl`, `enum.tpl`, `resource.tpl` and
`sandbox.tpl` define blocks shared by the module files and `sandbox.d.ts`, so a
type reads the same in both. To change the output, edit a template, run
`just generate`, and commit the regenerated example: the golden test fails until
they match.

## Documentation

Every comment in the protos is carried into JSDoc, in the module files and in
`sandbox.d.ts`, so editors and the model read the same text:

- leading and trailing comments on messages, fields, oneofs, enums, enum
  values, services and RPCs, dedented, paragraphs kept;
- the comment above `package`, as the package `index.ts` module doc
  (`@packageDocumentation`);
- `mcp.v1` descriptions and codemode `instructions`, added after the comment
  rather than replacing it;
- `deprecated = true`, as `@deprecated`;
- AIP-192 references such as `[Book][library.v1.Book]`, as their text;
- notes derived from annotations: required, output only, resource names,
  oneof members, 64-bit integers, bytes and well-known type formats.

## Parsing

`protogen` reads the request; protokit's service IR
([`protokit/service`](https://github.com/the-protobuf-project/protokit/tree/main/service))
reads the AIP vocabulary: `google.api.http` bindings, `google.api.resource`
patterns, `resource_reference` and `field_behavior`. It also rejects invalid
HTTP rules and conflicting routes, the same way other protokit plugins do.
[`aip.go`](../plugin/generator/aip.go) indexes that IR for the model build.
The generator itself reads only `codemode.v1`, the `mcp.v1` descriptions and
hints, and `buf.validate` required.

protokit's IR covers messages an RPC reaches and resources declared on
messages. `aip.go` adds file-level `google.api.resource_definition` entries,
plus `field_behavior` and `resource_reference` on messages that only a
snippet uses.

## Languages

The plugin takes a `lang` option, like `protoc-gen-mcp`: `typescript` (alias
`ts`) is the default and, for now, the only language; `all` expands to every
supported one, and anything else fails with the list of supported languages.

The model the generator builds (services, methods, approval, replay, revert,
resources, paths without extensions, well-known types by proto name) is
language-neutral. Each language is a `Language` in
[`languages.go`](../plugin/generator/languages.go) with its emitters in
`<lang>_*.go` and its layouts in `templates/<lang>/`, and its options in its
own section of `codemode.yaml` (`typescript:` today).

To add a host language, say Go once a Go Code Mode runtime exists:

1. Implement `Language` in `go_language.go` and add it to `languages`.
2. Write its emitters in `go_*.go`, mapping proto and well-known types to Go.
3. Put its layouts in `templates/go/*.tpl` and embed them.
4. Add a `go:` section to `Config` and the JSON Schema for its options.
5. Add an example and a golden test for its output.

Sandboxed code is JavaScript whatever the host, so every language describes the
sandbox API with the same TypeScript declarations (`sandbox.d.ts` and the
catalog's types); only the host side (codecs, clients, connectors, wiring)
changes per language.
